title: Knowledge-graph AI prioritizes TPP1 as a Parkinson’s disease target linked to α-synuclein homeostasis
summary: Standigm ASK’s knowledge-graph model ranked Parkinson’s disease target associations; subgraph enrichment and expression analyses narrowed 2,527 predicted targets to five candidates, including TPP1. In a human cell-based α-synuclein seeding model, TPP1 knockdown increased aggregate accumulation and insoluble α-synuclein, experimentally supporting a TPP1–α-synuclein relationship and a possible protective role.
ai_technology: Standigm ASK knowledge-graph path-based deep-learning model with subgraph-level over-representation re-ranking
organization: Standigm; and Ajou University School of Medicine

evidence.tested: In a human cell-based α-synuclein seeding model, TPP1 knockdown increased aggregate accumulation and insoluble α-synuclein, experimentally supporting a TPP1–α-synuclein relationship and a possible protective role.
evidence.unknown: The functional experiment is a human neuroblastoma cell model exposed to α-synuclein preformed fibrils, not a clinical or in-vivo therapeutic demonstration. Knockdown increasing aggregation supports a protective association; direct enzymatic cleavage of α-synuclein is proposed from structural modeling, not established by the reported work. TPP1 is a candidate therapeutic target, not a validated treatment.
evidence.ai_role: The model integrated heterogeneous biomedical databases, encoded relational paths using a convolutional network and attention aggregation, and produced disease-target scores. Researchers applied enrichment and transcriptomic filters to prioritize TPP1, then validated TPP1’s relationship to α-synuclein aggregation via siRNA knockdown and cellular assays; AlphaFold-Multimer modeling suggested, but did not prove, direct proteolysis.
